title: VRAM compressed textures with editor variant fail to load
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in 4.5-beta1 and 4.4.1-stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta1 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

If a texture resource's import settings has both

1) _Compress Mode_ set to "VRAM Compressed" (the default for 3D projects); and
2) has an editor variant (at least one of _Scale With Editor_ or _Convert Colors_ is enabled)

the texture will fail to load. If a scene is open that uses the texture, an error is immediately printed: `Unable to open file: res://.godot/imported/icon.svg-218a8f2b3041327d8a5756f3a245f83b.s3tc.editor.ctex.`. After a project reload you might get a broken dependency popup window, and textures or custom icons that visibly haven't loaded in properly.

It looks like Godot is trying to load the editor variant with a `*.s3tc.editor.ctex` suffix, but it was saved without the image compress format as just `*.editor.ctex`.

### Steps to reproduce

In the attached MRP, just enable _Scale With Editor_ and/or _Convert Colors_ in the import settings of `icon.svg`.

In general:

- In the import settings of a texture used in the current scene (either in-game or as an editor icon), set _Compress Mode_ to "VRAM Compressed"
- Enable _Scale With Editor_ and/or _Convert Colors_ in the same import settings
- Click reimport
- Immediately observe the error
- Reload current project for more errors

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[editor-variant-vram-compressed_2025-06-26_22-10-51.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20933050/editor-variant-vram-compressed_2025-06-26_22-10-51.zip)
